clue.text: Line in order shortened for gardening implement

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
shortened says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to order someone to do something is to tell them
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A gardener arranges tools in a tidy row, one cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is the verb, to instruct; 'shortened' takes its last letter, then 'in' sets the line inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool with a scoop-shaped blade used for planting and digging.

clue.text: Papers exhibit this kind, fine expert

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Newspapers show off a fine expert of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first three words: every newspaper displays its print in some font.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is the printed font style that newspapers display on every page.

clue.text: Opening plain remedy to banish cold

parts.note: overt means plain, out in the open

indicators.note: to banish says the cold letter is sent away from the remedy word

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: An unfussy treatment that sees off a cold makes a promising start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to banish' removes C from CURE, leaving URE.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is the opening piece of an opera or the first approach in a negotiation.

clue.text: Extremely educated geek occasionally gets head start

indicators.note: Extremely points to the outermost letters, first and last, of the next word
occasionally means taking only every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A highly educated geek sometimes gets ahead of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes ED from educated; 'occasionally' takes GE from geek.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is an advantage, a head start over rivals.

clue.text: One working in lobby with assistance gets the advantage

parts.note: a whip is the party official who herds MPs through the voting lobbies in Parliament
to give a hand is to give assistance

explanation.surface: A political lobbyist who gets help ends up in the stronger position.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, MPs vote by walking through division lobbies, and party whips make sure they go the right way.
explanation.definitionFit: To have the whip hand is an idiom for holding control or the upper position.

clue.text: Husband brought rail out as a guide for sailors

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband carried a rail outside to help sailors find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles BROUGHTRAIL after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour light is a lamp marking a port's entrance to guide vessels in at night.

clue.text: Extra note about ordinary day in schools

indicators.note: about says the extra note wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a PS is a postscript, an extra note at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A school adds a postscript about an ordinary day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' is not about education: it is the plural of a school of fish or whales.
explanation.definitionFit: Pods are groups of whales or dolphins, just as schools are groups of fish.

clue.text: A country in which university replaces American? That's wise

indicators.note: replaces says the university letter is swapped in for the American letter in the country word

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A country where academics take over from Americans would be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' is a state, not a named nation; 'replaces' swaps its American letter for the university one.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and perceptive, a close synonym of wise.

clue.text: Undaunted lawyer in New York perhaps on call

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A fearless New York lawyer is always on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes someone bold and unafraid, so it can stand for undaunted.

clue.text: Page in front of shelf showing undertaking

indicators.note: in front of says the page letter comes before the shelf word

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A page placed before a shelf reveals some project.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise, which is one sense of undertaking.

clue.text: Jaguar, say, with top and rear manufactured around Germany

indicators.note: around says the rebuilt letters go round the other piece
manufactured means made up or fabricated, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car with its top and rear made around Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' shuffles TOPREAR into PREATOR, and 'around' puts D inside it. 'Jaguar' looks like the car, but it is the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaguar is a hunting big cat, an example of a predator.

clue.text: In favour of article with piece of music to put things straight

parts.note: for means in favour of
the is the definite article
a record is a recorded piece of music

explanation.surface: Supporting a newspaper article with a tune to clear up a misunderstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something for the record sets the facts down officially to correct any misunderstanding.

clue.text: Something bound to happen in garden party, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor party or fair, often held in a garden

explanation.surface: A garden party that is inevitable, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fundraising fair with stalls and games.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is destiny, the course of events that cannot be avoided.

clue.text: Element in benefit about right

indicators.note: about says the benefit word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing

explanation.surface: Part of a benefit relates to what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, number five on the periodic table.

clue.text: Surprise enthusiasts making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: nuts are fanatics or enthusiasts, as in health nuts

explanation.surface: Fans are astonished when their heroes return.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or amaze, a verb synonym of surprise.

clue.text: Quickly leave chap principally covered in black powder

indicators.note: covered in says that letter is enclosed by the powder word

parts.note: soot is the black powder left by burning

indicators.note: principally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep, covered in soot, makes a hasty exit.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoot is informal for to dash off or depart in a hurry.

clue.text: Very pale wash enjoyed? Not altogether!

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bath was enjoyed, and the answer is no, not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey like ash, through shock or illness.

clue.text: One distorting features?

parts.note: reads like a vandal or a liar, but describes an artist who exaggerates faces for comic effect

explanation.surface: Someone who twists the facts in news stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' suggests newspaper articles, but it means facial features.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricaturist draws people with exaggerated facial traits for humorous effect.

clue.text: More safe after revolution that's frightening

indicators.note: after revolution means the letters have been turned about and reorganised

explanation.surface: Things got safer after the uprising, which is scary.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means causing fear or dread, so it is a synonym of frightening.

clue.text: Actor Dominic boarding very large railway in Shropshire town

indicators.note: boarding says the actor's name gets on board, between the size letters and the railway letters

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
Dominic West is the English actor from The Wire

explanation.surface: Dominic West takes an outsize train to a town in Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarding' puts the actor between the size and the railway. Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswestry is a market town in north-west Shropshire near Wales.

clue.text: Curiously Eve is chosen with son to show unity

indicators.note: curiously suggests something strange, so the letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, Eve is picked alongside her son to demonstrate family solidarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously' shuffles all of 'Eve is chosen'; the son's letter follows at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesiveness is the quality of sticking together, a close synonym for unity.

clue.text: Abandon opportunity when leaving hotel to overlook lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overlook puts the first piece above the second
when leaving says the hotel letter departs from the opportunity word

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Give up the chance of a hotel with a lake view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when leaving' drops H from CHANCE, leaving CANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a plan is to abandon or call it off.

clue.text: Rank obtained by Scottish island over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

explanation.surface: A military rank awarded by a Scottish island community over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a noun for a grade, but it is the adjective meaning utter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant and rank both mean complete or utter, as in an arrant fool.

clue.text: Spacious place producing pints first off

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a dairy produces milk, sold by the pint

explanation.surface: A roomy pub, the first place to serve pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pints' suggests beer, but it is milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy describes a room that is open, light and roomy.

clue.text: Nerdy English companion enthralled by empty toy

indicators.note: enthralled by says the other letters are held inside the emptied word
empty says the middle is removed, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An English friend captivated by a gadget with no batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the ends of toy; 'enthralled by' holds English and the Companion of Honour inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Techy is informal for someone keen on technology, much like nerdy or geeky.

clue.text: Firm even at intervals lacking regulation?

indicators.note: at intervals says only every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A company that is steady now and then might lack rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes F, R, E and E from 'Firm even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Free can mean unrestricted or deregulated, as in a free market without controls.

clue.text: Detect roundish mark

definitions.meaning: a small round mark or blemish

explanation.definitionFit: Spot is both a verb for noticing and a noun for a small round blemish.

clue.text: A criticism held up soldier

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: rap is slang for blame or criticism, as in taking the rap

explanation.surface: A soldier delayed by a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A para is a paratrooper, a soldier trained to drop by parachute.

clue.text: Vigorously support former jockey

definitions.meaning: to ... a cause is to back it vigorously
A retired jockey who won the 1981 Grand National on Aldaniti

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion is a verb for advocating a cause and the surname of jockey Bob Champion.

clue.text: Seasoned dish giving artist uncomfortable condition

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: A spicy meal giving a painter a painful ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: A flier entering terrible duel needs breathing space

indicators.note: entering says the first pieces go inside the jumbled word
terrible suggests the letters are badly mangled and reordered

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, so a flier

explanation.surface: A bird caught up in an awful fight needs room to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' shuffles DUEL to LUDE, and 'entering' puts ATIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom or leeway, room to act, like breathing space.

clue.text: Stephen, maybe, encapsulates a king close to grotesque deception

indicators.note: encapsulates says the surname wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Stephen Fry is the English comic actor and writer
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry plays a king in a grotesque piece of trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fakery is the practice of faking things, a form of deception or fraud.
